subject: Access to SKS Swaminarayan Temple – CPZ and School Street concerns
body:
Dear Councillor,

I am writing to you as a constituent and a regular attendee of SKS Swaminarayan Temple Woolwich on St Margaret's Grove.

I understand the Council wants safer, less congested streets, and I support those aims. However, I am concerned that the proposed Controlled Parking Zone and the School Street scheme, taken together, will make it much harder for our congregation to attend. Many of our members are elderly, disabled or young families who rely on a car to get to the temple.

As the parking orders have not yet been made, there is still time to get this right. I would be grateful if you could raise these concerns with the Cabinet Member for Transport, and let me know his response in writing.

Thank you for your time.

Yours sincerely,

[Your name]

subject: Request for a balanced approach on St Margaret's Grove parking
body:
Dear Councillor,

As one of your residents who worships at SKS Swaminarayan Temple Woolwich, I would like to share my concerns about the parking and traffic changes planned for St Margaret's Grove.

The proposed CPZ would apply seven days a week, including the weekends when the temple is busiest. Alongside the School Street restrictions, this could make the temple difficult to reach for those who need it most.

I am not asking the Council to abandon its plans, only to find a fairer balance. Could you please support shorter controlled hours on the Grove, with weekends left free, before the orders are finalised?

I would welcome your view on this.

Kind regards,

[Your name]

subject: Equality impact of parking changes near Woolwich temple
body:
Dear Councillor,

I attend SKS Swaminarayan Temple Woolwich and live in the borough. I am writing about the proposed CPZ on St Margaret's Grove and the School Street scheme on the same road.

Our congregation includes many older and disabled people for whom walking a long distance, or paying to park every visit, is a real barrier to worship. I was told that a full Equalities Impact Assessment would be completed before the parking orders are made.

Could you please ask for that assessment to be published so the community can see how our needs have been considered? I would also appreciate a written reply to this email.

With thanks,

[Your name]

subject: Please raise the temple parking issue on our behalf
body:
Dear Councillor,

I hope you are well. I am one of many local residents who attend SKS Swaminarayan Temple Woolwich, and I wanted to make you aware of how worried our community is about the planned parking controls and School Street on St Margaret's Grove.

The temple is a place of worship and a community hub for families, older people and volunteers. These changes risk making it harder for people to take part in everyday religious and community life.

I would simply ask that you raise this as an issue with the relevant Cabinet Member and officers, so our concerns are heard before final decisions are taken.

Many thanks,

[Your name]

subject: Festival days and the proposed St Margaret's Grove CPZ
body:
Dear Councillor,

I am writing as a borough resident and temple attendee about the proposed Controlled Parking Zone and School Street on St Margaret's Grove.

Throughout the year our temple holds festivals and special events that bring many families together. Under the current proposals, visitors on these days would face restrictions and charges that could discourage attendance, particularly for elderly and disabled worshippers.

Would you support the Council agreeing parking suspensions on our main festival and religious days? I believe this would be a fair and practical step.

Thank you for considering this.

Yours sincerely,

[Your name]

subject: Concerns from a constituent about access to my place of worship
body:
Dear Councillor,

I am contacting you because I am concerned about my ability, and that of my fellow worshippers, to continue attending SKS Swaminarayan Temple Woolwich once the planned changes on St Margaret's Grove come in.

The CPZ and the School Street are presented as separate schemes, but for those of us travelling to the temple they will be felt together. I appreciate the reasons behind them, but I hope the Council can also consider the impact on a long-established faith community.

I would be grateful if you could take this up with the Cabinet Member for Transport and ask whether the controlled hours on the Grove could be reduced before the orders are made.

Kind regards,

[Your name]

subject: Parking permits for places of worship – a suggestion
body:
Dear Councillor,

As a resident and regular visitor to SKS Swaminarayan Temple Woolwich, I wanted to raise the proposed parking controls on St Margaret's Grove with you.

I understand that some other London boroughs allow religious organisations to buy a limited number of parking permits for volunteers and those who need them most. Something similar here could ease the pressure on our congregation without undermining the Council's goals.

Could you please raise this idea with officers, and let me know in writing whether it could be considered?

With best wishes,

[Your name]

subject: St Margaret's Grove: CPZ hours and weekend worship
body:
Dear Councillor,

I live in Royal Greenwich and attend SKS Swaminarayan Temple Woolwich. I am writing about the CPZ planned for St Margaret's Grove.

I notice that other streets in the same scheme are only controlled on weekdays during working hours. The temple's busiest times are evenings and weekends, so seven-day controls will fall heaviest on worshippers rather than commuters.

I would ask you to support weekend exemption for the Grove before the parking orders are made. Alongside this, the School Street scheme should take account of access for older and disabled attendees.

Thank you for reading.

Yours sincerely,

[Your name]

subject: A request to meet the temple community
body:
Dear Councillor,

I am a constituent and an attendee of SKS Swaminarayan Temple Woolwich. Many of us are concerned about the upcoming parking restrictions and School Street on St Margaret's Grove and how they will affect our ability to worship together.

We would value the chance to explain our situation in person. Would you be willing to meet representatives of the temple community to hear our concerns before these schemes are finalised?

I look forward to hearing from you.

Kind regards,

[Your name]

subject: Young families and the planned parking changes
body:
Dear Councillor,

I am writing as a local resident and member of the congregation at SKS Swaminarayan Temple Woolwich.

Our temple supports families with young children through classes, activities and a nursery. With both a CPZ and a School Street proposed on St Margaret's Grove, parents may find it harder and more costly to bring children to these activities.

I fully support safer streets for children. I only ask that the needs of families using the temple are considered too. Please could you raise this with the Cabinet Member and share his response with me?

Thank you,

[Your name]

subject: Volunteers at Woolwich temple and the proposed CPZ
body:
Dear Councillor,

I hope this email finds you well. I live in the borough and regularly attend SKS Swaminarayan Temple Woolwich, where many people volunteer their time to run services and community activities.

Volunteers often spend several hours at the temple, and under the proposed CPZ on St Margaret's Grove they would have to pay to park for the whole of that time. Combined with the School Street restrictions, I worry this will discourage the people who keep the temple running.

Could you please ask whether the Council would consider permits for the temple's volunteers, or shorter controlled hours on the Grove?

With thanks,

[Your name]

subject: Please consider a review of the St Margaret's Grove scheme
body:
Dear Councillor,

I am one of your constituents and I worship at SKS Swaminarayan Temple Woolwich. I would like to share my concerns about the CPZ and School Street proposals for St Margaret's Grove.

I understand the Council has said it will monitor the parking scheme and review it if there is a disproportionate impact. I would ask you to support a formal review of the Grove after the first few months, with the temple community consulted as part of it.

I would also be grateful for a written reply setting out your view.

Yours sincerely,

[Your name]

subject: Elderly worshippers and access to the temple
body:
Dear Councillor,

I am writing about the planned parking controls and School Street on St Margaret's Grove, which I believe will particularly affect the older members of our temple community.

Many elderly worshippers at SKS Swaminarayan Temple Woolwich are driven by family members and cannot walk long distances. Being dropped off quickly is not always practical for someone with limited mobility.

I respectfully ask you to raise this issue with the Council and to make sure the needs of older and disabled worshippers are properly considered before any final decision.

Kind regards,

[Your name]

subject: Constituent query: Equalities Impact Assessment for Woolwich CPZ
body:
Dear Councillor,

As a Greenwich resident who attends SKS Swaminarayan Temple Woolwich, I would like to ask about the equality assessment for the proposed CPZ on St Margaret's Grove.

Has the full Equalities Impact Assessment been completed? If so, could it be shared? If not, could you please ask that it is completed and published before the parking orders are made, and that it also considers the School Street proposal on the same road?

Thank you for your help with this.

Best wishes,

[Your name]

subject: Finding a fair compromise on temple parking
body:
Dear Councillor,

I am a member of the SKS Swaminarayan Temple Woolwich congregation and a resident of the borough.

I recognise that parking pressure is a genuine issue for people living nearby, and I am not opposed to sensible controls. However, the current CPZ and School Street proposals for St Margaret's Grove seem to leave little room for a community that has been part of the area for many years.

I believe a compromise is possible, for example controls limited to weekday hours. I would be grateful if you could raise this with the Cabinet Member before the orders are made.

Thank you for your consideration.

Yours sincerely,

[Your name]

subject: Impact of parking charges on regular worship
body:
Dear Councillor,

I attend SKS Swaminarayan Temple Woolwich several times a week, as do many others in our community. I am writing about the proposed CPZ on St Margaret's Grove.

For regular worshippers, paying to park on every visit will quickly add up. For some families and pensioners this cost may mean attending less often, which would be a real loss to them and to the community.

Please could you raise this with the Council and ask that the cost to regular worshippers is taken into account, along with the effect of the School Street scheme on access?

Kind regards,

[Your name]

subject: Disabled worshippers and the St Margaret's Grove proposals
body:
Dear Councillor,

I am writing as a borough resident and temple attendee to raise the needs of disabled members of our congregation at SKS Swaminarayan Temple Woolwich.

Not everyone with a disability holds a Blue Badge, and many rely on being driven close to the entrance. The planned CPZ and School Street on St Margaret's Grove could make the temple much harder for them to reach.

I would ask you to raise this with the relevant Cabinet Member, and to make sure the Council's Public Sector Equality Duty is properly met before any decision is finalised.

Thank you,

[Your name]

subject: Please share our concerns with the Cabinet Member for Transport
body:
Dear Councillor,

I am a local resident and attendee at SKS Swaminarayan Temple Woolwich.

I would like to add my voice to the concerns about the proposed parking controls and School Street on St Margaret's Grove. Our temple serves people of all ages, and these changes risk making it harder for many to attend.

As our ward councillor, I would be grateful if you could pass these concerns on to the Cabinet Member for Transport, and let me know his reply.

Many thanks for your support.

Yours sincerely,

[Your name]

subject: Temple community concerns ahead of CPZ decision
body:
Dear Councillor,

I hope you are keeping well. I am writing to raise concerns shared by many families who attend SKS Swaminarayan Temple Woolwich about the changes planned for St Margaret's Grove.

The temple is more than a place of prayer. It offers support to older people, activities for children and a space for the community to come together. The CPZ and School Street proposals could put some of this at risk if access becomes too difficult or costly.

I would simply ask you to raise this as an issue with the Council, so our community's needs are part of the discussion before the orders are made.

With kind regards,

[Your name]

subject: School Street on St Margaret's Grove – access for worshippers
body:
Dear Councillor,

As a resident of Royal Greenwich and regular visitor to SKS Swaminarayan Temple Woolwich, I am writing about the School Street proposed for St Margaret's Grove, as well as the planned CPZ.

I support measures that keep children safe. However, the School Street hours overlap with times when older worshippers arrive at the temple, and it is not clear what arrangements there will be for them.

Could you please ask the Council to ensure that suitable access arrangements for elderly and disabled worshippers are included in the final decision? I would appreciate a written reply.

Thank you,

[Your name]

subject: Shorter controlled hours for St Margaret's Grove
body:
Dear Councillor,

I live in the borough and attend SKS Swaminarayan Temple Woolwich. I am writing about the proposed Controlled Parking Zone on St Margaret's Grove.

The proposed hours run from morning to evening every day of the week. Shorter controls, aimed at the times when commuter parking is actually a problem, would protect residents while still allowing worshippers to visit.

I would be grateful if you could support shorter hours on the Grove and raise this with the Cabinet Member before the parking orders are made.

Kind regards,

[Your name]

subject: Keeping our temple accessible to everyone
body:
Dear Councillor,

I am a constituent writing about the planned parking controls and School Street on St Margaret's Grove, where SKS Swaminarayan Temple Woolwich is located.

Our temple welcomes everyone, whatever their age, ability or income. I worry that charging to park and restricting vehicle access will mean that some people simply stop coming, particularly those who are already isolated.

Please could you raise this with the Council and ask how it intends to keep the temple accessible to all? I would be grateful for a written response.

Yours sincerely,

[Your name]

subject: Raising an issue affecting your constituents at the Woolwich temple
body:
Dear Councillor,

I am writing to make you aware of an issue affecting many of your constituents who attend SKS Swaminarayan Temple Woolwich.

The proposed CPZ and School Street on St Margaret's Grove are causing real concern across our congregation, from young families to elderly worshippers and volunteers. We would like the Council to understand the effect these schemes could have on our community.

I would be grateful if you could raise this with officers and the Cabinet Member, and keep me updated on any response.

Thank you for your help.

Best regards,

[Your name]

subject: Suspension days for religious occasions at the temple
body:
Dear Councillor,

As a borough resident who worships at SKS Swaminarayan Temple Woolwich, I am writing about the proposed parking controls on St Margaret's Grove.

Our temple marks a number of important religious occasions each year, when attendance is much higher than usual. I would ask you to support an agreed number of parking suspension days for these occasions, so families can attend together without difficulty.

Could you also raise the wider impact of the CPZ and School Street with the Cabinet Member?

Thank you for your consideration.

Yours sincerely,

[Your name]

subject: Nursery families and the St Margaret's Grove changes
body:
Dear Councillor,

I am a resident of Royal Greenwich and part of the SKS Swaminarayan Temple Woolwich community. I am writing about the CPZ and School Street proposed for St Margaret's Grove.

The temple's nursery and children's activities are valued by local families. Parents dropping off and collecting young children need to be able to do so safely and without undue cost, and I am concerned the combined schemes will make this harder.

I would ask you to raise this with the Council and request that the impact on families using the temple is considered before the orders are made.

Kind regards,

[Your name]

subject: Weekend worship and the proposed parking controls
body:
Dear Councillor,

I attend SKS Swaminarayan Temple Woolwich, mostly at weekends, and live in the borough.

Weekends are when most families are able to come to the temple together. Under the proposed CPZ on St Margaret's Grove, parking would be controlled on Saturdays and Sundays as well, which I feel goes further than necessary.

I would be grateful if you could support leaving weekends free of controls on the Grove, and let me know your position in writing.

Thank you,

[Your name]

subject: Asking for our community's voice to be heard
body:
Dear Councillor,

I am writing as one of your residents and a member of the SKS Swaminarayan Temple Woolwich congregation.

Many of us responded to the consultation on parking in Woolwich, and we remain concerned about the CPZ and School Street planned for St Margaret's Grove. We feel our community's needs have not yet been fully reflected in the proposals.

I would ask you to raise our concerns with the Cabinet Member, and to support a meeting between the Council and temple representatives before the schemes go ahead.

Yours sincerely,

[Your name]

subject: Practical concerns about getting to the temple
body:
Dear Councillor,

I hope you are well. I am a borough resident and attend SKS Swaminarayan Temple Woolwich, and I wanted to share some practical concerns about the planned changes on St Margaret's Grove.

Public transport to the temple is limited, so many of us drive, often bringing older relatives or young children. Paid parking and School Street restrictions on the same road will make each visit more complicated.

Please could you raise this as an issue with the Council on our behalf?

With thanks,

[Your name]

subject: Request for a written response on the Woolwich CPZ
body:
Dear Councillor,

I am a constituent and worship at SKS Swaminarayan Temple Woolwich on St Margaret's Grove.

I am concerned about the proposed CPZ and School Street and the effect they will have on our congregation, especially older and disabled members. I would like to understand how the Council has weighed these concerns.

Could you please ask officers whether a review of the Grove's parking arrangements will take place after the scheme starts, and send me a written reply with their answer?

Thank you for your time.

Kind regards,

[Your name]

subject: Supporting both safer streets and access to worship
body:
Dear Councillor,

I am writing as a resident and attendee of SKS Swaminarayan Temple Woolwich about the proposals for St Margaret's Grove.

I believe it is possible to support safer, greener streets while also protecting people's ability to reach their place of worship. At the moment, the CPZ and School Street plans do not seem to strike that balance for our community.

I would be grateful if you could raise this with the Cabinet Member for Transport and ask that the published Equalities Impact Assessment addresses access to the temple.

Thank you for considering my concerns.

Yours sincerely,

[Your name]
